Resolves #21887

Containers & Layouts gets its three missing tiles:
- `container/accordion` is a shop's help center whose icons draw and whose `maxExpandedItems` is a live inspector control.
- `layout/card` is a three-step setup wizard, driven by Back and Next from pointer or keyboard.
- `container/fragment` moves onto the workbench: a shipping form groups its address in a Fragment, and a panel beside it lists the form's DOM children, read from the page, so a visitor sees that no wrapper element exists.

All three open on the catalog's theme. Their records sit in `layouts.json` with crop pairs on neomjs/pages#186.

The renewal ran into three engine defects, fixed here (see the Deltas). The accordion's `maxExpandedItems` was not reactive. Its header icons overlapped their titles. Moving a Fragment threw wherever the browser has `moveBefore()`.

Evidence: L3 (drives of the three examples against a local server in four themes at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844, new e2e, unit and component tests, the tile camera) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-4 are interaction and rendering in a browser).

## Deltas from ticket

- `Neo.container.Accordion#maxExpandedItems` is reactive now. It was read only when an item opened, and compared with `===`. Lowering it left every item open, and once more items were open than the cap, the next open closed none. `collapseOverflow()` closes the items opened first until the rest fit. It serves both the new `afterSetMaxExpandedItems()` and `childExpandChange()`. A positive cap counts whole items: `beforeSetMaxExpandedItems()` rounds it down, to one at the least, since the item about to open always opens. Euclid's probe showed a 0.5 cap looping forever on the first open. Four unit tests in `test/playwright/unit/container/Accordion.spec.mjs`; the lower-cap and fractional ones are red before their changes. The existing keyboard test in `AccordionModel.spec.mjs` caught a stale-copy bug on the way (the `expandedItems` getter hands out a copy).
- The accordion item's header icon kept its 10 px / 15 px spacing on its `::before`, inside a 20 px box, so a wide glyph drew over the title's first letter, in every theme. The spacing sits on the icon's own box now (`resources/css/src/container/AccordionItem.css`).
- `Neo.main.DeltaUpdates#moveNode` packed a Fragment's comment-anchored range into a `DocumentFragment` and handed it to `moveBefore()`, which takes none. The call threw a `HierarchyRequestError`, and the range, already appended to the `DocumentFragment`, left the page. Where the browser has `moveBefore()` the range now moves node by node, each node keeping its state. `test/playwright/component/container/FragmentMove.spec.mjs` moves a whole range, red before the change. It is its own file because `FragmentDeltaUpdates.spec.mjs` carries trailing whitespace the commit hook refuses.
- The wizard's summary sets `text`, not `html`: a typed name like `Lighthouse <Studio>` became an element. The new wizard test is red before that change.
- The tiles take their size from their examples. The tile list in `buildScripts/docs/captureExamples.json` is frozen since #21908, so the three capture rows are gone. The wizard is 240 high, the size its row gave the camera.
- On a phone the stage shrinks the wizard to about 180 px, because the wizard clips its overflow for the card slide. In the first frames its text field ran 1 px under the button bar. Below 600 px a step's top padding and gaps tighten.
- An accordion item opens by its arrow; a click on its title selects it. That is the engine's design, left alone, and the record's `lookFor` says so.
- The fragment's tile crop shows the form alone. The camera crops the stage component, and the DOM panel is a stage item; the tile's name and feature line carry the fragment.
